messages:
ben_customer_ops: Hey team — our integration started failing after we upgraded the TS SDK. Embeddings requests intermittently return 400 'dimension mismatch' for vectors that used to work. Seen ~10% of calls fail, others succeed. Started ~2026-03-16 18:23 UTC.

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting that — can you share the request payload (headers + body) and the exact error text? Also which model and SDK version? :eyes: 

ben_customer_ops: Model: text-embed-003-v1 (pinned). SDK: @redwood/ts-embed 2.1.0 -> we just moved from 2.0.3. Error: `400 Bad Request {"error":"dimension mismatch: got 1536, expected 1024"}`. Our stored vectors are 1536; we didn't change them.

alex_support: Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) Are you sure the model changed? 2) Any proxies or middleware that could re-encode body?

ben_customer_ops: Model pinned in our config, didn't change. No proxies that touch payload. We see occasional 500 timeouts too, and the TS client has been retrying which caused duplicate documents to be indexed upstream.

maya_engineer: Interesting — sounds like a model fallback or routing to a different model variant (1024 dim) when capacity is constrained. Our routing can fall back to smaller variants which would cause dim mismatch. Can you paste the full request headers (redact API key) and the SDK call?

ben_customer_ops: Header snippet: `Content-Type: application/json`, `x-client-version: myapp/1.2.3`, `x-redwood-model: text-embed-003-v1` (we set that). TS call: 
```ts
const v = await client.embeddings.create({
  model: 'text-embed-003-v1',
  input: ['doc1', 'doc2'],
  batch_size: 32
});
```
Errors are non-deterministic, e.g. succeed, then fail a minute later.

joel_sdk: From SDK side — 2.1.0 introduced an internal routing header change: we added `x-rw-prefer-low-cost` when caller sets `optimize: 'cost'` (we auto-detect for some configs). That shouldn't be on by default. Do you set any optimization flags? Also we changed default chunking which affects how batch payloads are shaped.

ben_customer_ops: We don't set optimize flags. We do call `client.config.set({ autoOptimize: true })` in an init path though (legacy). Could that flip the header?

joel_sdk: Ah that explains it — autoOptimize toggles the header in 2.1.0. If routing picks a lower-cost variant in another region due to that header, you'll hit the 1024-dim model. We need to be explicit about routing defaults. For now, can you force model_id in the request to the exact canonical id? The server-side honor should be strict.

alex_support: While we triage routing, let's also address timeouts and retry duplicates. ben: what's your SDK retry/backoff config? Are you using the default exponential backoff?

ben_customer_ops: Default retries. We saw bursts during peak traffic and the client increases concurrency to 64 (we use parallel batches). We got a billing spike because retries re-submitted batches.

maya_engineer: Two recommended immediate mitigations: 1) Set `autoOptimize: false` or upgrade to SDK 2.1.1 (we'll cut a patch) that stops sending `x-rw-prefer-low-cost` unless explicitly enabled. 2) Reduce client-side max concurrency to 8 and set `maxRetries: 2` with jittered backoff. That will reduce duplicate submissions.

joel_sdk: Patch notes: 2.1.1 will: not send routing header by default, fix batch chunking edge-case for single vs multi-input arrays (which could generate malformed shape metadata), and add an opt-in `strictModelId` flag that sets `x-rw-enforce-model` header to avoid transparent fallbacks.

ryan_infra: From infra: we rolled a capacity-shift yesterday in us-east-1 between 18:00–18:30 UTC which temporarily moved traffic to alternative pools. That could explain fallback to a 1024-dim variant in the fallback pool. We're rolling a capacity corrective now.

ben_customer_ops: OK will set autoOptimize false and throttle concurrency. Can you confirm whether the server should have rejected a mismatched-dim request with 400 vs doing silent fallback? We prefer strict rejection to avoid silent data problems.

maya_engineer: Agree — we should surface an explicit routing hint in the error: `model_mismatch: routed_to_variant text-embed-003-small (dim=1024)`. Filing an internal ticket to make the error clearer. For now, use `strictModelId: true` once SDK patch is out, or pass `x-rw-enforce-model` header.

ben_customer_ops: Quick repro logs I can share: I can paste a failing curl if you want.

alex_support: Please do a minimal curl that reproduces the 400 and attach. Also include your token redacted. That will help infra trace routing decisions with request ids. :thumbsup:

ben_customer_ops: Curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-003-v1","input":["a short doc"],"batch_size":1}'
```
Response: `400 Bad Request {"error":"dimension mismatch: got 1536, expected 1024","request_id":"req_9f3b"}`

ryan_infra: Got request_id=req_9f3b — checked routing logs: that request was routed to fallback pool in eu-west-1 which hosts text-embed-003-small. I can trace why region mismatch happened if you include the full request headers.

ben_customer_ops: Headers attached in DM to alex.

joel_sdk: We'll push 2.1.1 tonight with the opt-in strictModelId flag and the autoOptimize default change. After that, please test again and report if any 400s persist.

alex_support: I'll keep this thread open and update when patch is released and infra stabilizes capacity. Thanks for the quick repro and logs — moving to high priority. :rocket:

deploy_bot: deploy started: infra/route-fix v2026.03.17-01 (triggered by ryan_infra)

alex_support: Follow-ups: once patched, please run 1000 small embedding requests with concurrency=8 and report fail rate. We'll refund any accidental duplicate billing while we triage.

ben_customer_ops: Will do tests tonight and report numbers. Appreciate the help!
